subject: Post-demo: Clarify prompt/output storage, retention options, and next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@veridianhealth.com>, Rafael Rogers <rafael.rogers@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap & PII storage options (short answers)

Hi Emma / Rafael — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap of the storage/retention items you asked about and proposed next steps. I pulled the key points from the session to keep this tight.

Summary (short):
- What we store: by default Redwood hosted endpoints persist minimal telemetry (request metadata, model+version, timestamps). Prompt and output payloads are NOT stored persistently unless you opt into logging for debugging or quality monitoring.
- Default retention: if logging is enabled, prompt/output payloads are retained for 30 days in our secure object store (configurable).
- Residency: hosted logs are stored in a US region (us-west-2) for accounts on the US plan; we can route to a specific region on Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Access controls & encryption: all stored payloads are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS) on Private; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default. Role-based access and audit logs are available.
- Logging controls: you can turn on/off payload logging per route or per model. We support sampling rules and redaction hooks to strip defined PHI fields before storage.
- Private options: Dedicated reservations or Private (VPC/on-prem) allow zero-persistence mode (no prompt/output storage) and bring-your-own-key.

Attachments: I attached a one-pager that summarizes these modes and an example retention table (redwood-data-handling-onepager.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica to send a concise tech note with exact TTL/legal language for procurement (she's cc'd).
2) Veridian to confirm whether you need zero-persistence for any environment or if 30-day TTL with redaction policies is fine.
3) If zero-persistence required, we schedule a short architecture call to scope Private/Dedicated timeline and cost.

Can you confirm which of the three options below matches your needs so we can scope?
A) Hosted with 30-day TTL + redaction
B) Hosted with sampled logging + 90-day retention (longer analytics)
C) Zero-persistence (Private/Dedicated) with BYOK

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber

From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@veridianhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & PII storage options (short answers)

Thanks, Jonas — very helpful summary. Two clarifications from our side:

1) For the pilot we want to avoid storing PHI at all. Our legal team called out that even short-lived storage of patient identifiers is a blocker unless it's strictly necessary. We expect option C (zero-persistence) is the target, but we need to understand the timeline and any limitations for pilot features (e.g., streaming, tool-calls).

2) On redaction hooks: can Redwood support server-side redaction rules that run before any persistence (not client-side)? We asked for examples where customers define a JSON schema of fields to drop — would that be sufficient to pass initial legal review?

Rafael (cc) will coordinate procurement questions — Rafael, could you confirm if we need a SOC 2 Type II attestation on file before we proceed with a pilot?

Thanks — Emma

Hi Emma / Rafael — Monica here (Security & Privacy engineering). Thanks for the clear asks — below are concrete answers and a couple of configuration examples we can implement immediately for your pilot.

Short answers:
- Zero-persistence pilot: Yes, we can enable a zero-persistence mode at the account or route level on Dedicated or Private deployments. In hosted mode we can mimic zero-persistence by turning off payload logging and enforcing server-side redaction, but some minimal telemetry (non-PII metadata) will remain for billing and SLOs. For a true zero-persistence guarantee (no payloads ever written to disk), Private or on-prem is required.
- Server-side redaction: Yes. We support server-side redaction hooks that run in the request pipeline before any payload reaches storage. You can supply a redaction schema (JSONPath/regex-based rules) or choose our pre-built healthcare PHI profile. We'll provide examples.
- SOC 2: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II. I'll attach our attestation and the compliance pack after this thread.

Configuration examples for pilot (option C preferred):
1) Private (recommended for Veridian pilot): deploy Redwood Private in your VPC; enable BYOK via your KMS; set payload_persistence=false; enable server_redaction_profile=veridian_phi; sampling=0. This will ensure no prompts/outputs are written to our hosted stores.
2) Hosted mimic (if you need faster spin-up): account-level payload_persistence=false; server_redaction_profile=veridian_phi; however, non-PII telemetry (latency, token counts, errors) will still be recorded for monitoring. We can purge telemetry after 7 days on request.

Attachments: redwood-data-handling-onepager.pdf (contains the two config snippets above) and a sample redaction schema (veridian-mvp-map.xlsx) for mapping fields you flagged in the demo.

Next operational steps:
- Rafael: confirm whether procurement requires a signed DPA and whether SOC 2 attestation and data processing addendum are sufficient.
- Jonas / Aditya: let's schedule a 30-minute architecture call if Veridian confirms Private for pilot — we'll bring infra and security to scope timeline (expect 2-3 weeks for a basic Private deployment with network setup).

Happy to hop on a call early next week.

Best,
